transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess the main thing is… my head just hasn’t felt clear lately. Like, foggy, kind of slow, and it’s bothering me because I’m usually pretty on top of things at work. I’m a personal care aide, so I have to keep track of what I’m doing and write client notes, and lately I’ve been catching these little mistakes—nothing huge, but enough that I notice. I’ll write something down wrong or leave out a detail, or I’ll walk into a room and suddenly forget what I was about to do.

It’s just not like me, and it’s making me nervous because my work depends on me being careful. That’s really what brought me in.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah… I have. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything, and I can still go to work and talk to people and do what I’m supposed to do, so from the outside I probably seem mostly normal. But lately when I wake up, there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like before I even get going, I already feel kind of weighed down.

It’s hard to explain because I can still function, but inside I feel sad and flat a lot of the time. Like I’m going through the motions during my shift, saying the right things to clients, doing the tasks, but underneath it there’s this dull sadness just sitting there.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I’d say it’s been about a month now. Maybe a little more, maybe a little less—I’m not great at pinning down the exact day it started—but for around four weeks this low feeling has just kind of been hanging over me.

It’s not constant every single second, but it’s been there most days… that heavy, guilty, foggy kind of feeling. Like I keep thinking I should be doing better or handling things better, and then my head feels cloudy on top of that. So yeah, about a month is probably the best way to put it.
Have you noticed any decrease in interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed a clear drop in that, honestly. I mean… I haven’t really been paying close attention to whether things are less enjoyable. I can’t think of a specific hobby or something where I’m like, “I used to love that and now I don’t.”

It’s more that I’ve been preoccupied with feeling foggy and kind of low, so maybe I’m not as tuned in to what I enjoy. But I wouldn’t say there’s been some obvious thing where I stopped caring about everything I normally like. At least not that I can clearly point to.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I don’t weigh myself regularly, so I can’t give you a number or anything like that. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different, at least not that I’ve noticed, and nobody’s said anything to me about looking like I’ve lost or gained weight.

I mean, day to day I don’t pay a ton of attention to it unless something feels tight or loose, and nothing has really jumped out at me recently. So… I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed any major change, but I can’t say I’ve been tracking it closely.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?

Yeah… I have, actually. More than I think makes sense for what I’m doing.

Like, even on days where I’m not doing a whole lot, my body just feels kind of worn out. Not sleepy exactly all the time, but drained, like I’ve already had a long day when I haven’t. And with my work, I’m used to being on my feet and helping people with basic care, so I know what normal tired feels like. But lately even something like helping a client shower takes more out of me than it should. I’ll finish and feel like I need to sit down for a while.

Even carrying groceries in from the car feels heavier than it should, if that makes sense. It’s not like I can’t do it, I still do what I have to do, but it feels like everything costs more energy than it used to.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about things that you wouldn't normally feel that way about?

Yeah… that one, yes. I don’t know if “worthless” is exactly the word I’d use, but guilty, definitely. I keep going back over things with my tío before he died, and it’s like my brain won’t let it rest.

I’ll think, why didn’t I call him more? Why didn’t I go visit sooner? I should’ve checked in, I should’ve made more time, I should’ve been there more as family. And I know, logically, people have work and life and you don’t always know how much time someone has, but that doesn’t really stop the feeling. It turns into this thing where I feel like I failed him somehow, like I didn’t do what I was supposed to do as his nephew.

It’s not constant every second, but when it hits, it feels heavier than normal guilt. Like I’m replaying the same few moments and judging myself over and over.
Have you been having thoughts of death or suicide?

I… yeah, I should probably be honest about that. I’m not making plans to hurt myself or anything like that. I don’t have something I’m preparing to do. But there have been mornings where I wake up and, before I even really get moving, I’ll have this thought like… if I hadn’t woken up, maybe that wouldn’t have been the worst thing.

And then I get scared by the fact that I even thought that, because I don’t want to die exactly. It’s more like wanting things to stop for a minute, or not having to feel everything when I first open my eyes. But no, I’m not planning to kill myself. It’s just those thoughts have been there sometimes, and I don’t like that they’re there.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get started on things than usual?

Yeah… I think so, though I notice it more as my body just not wanting to move, if that makes sense. Like even on days when I haven’t really done much, I feel worn out already. It’s not always that I’m sleepy, it’s more like I’m dragging myself through things.

At work, something pretty normal for me, like helping a client shower, has been taking more out of me than it should. I’ll do it, because I have to, but afterward I feel like I need to sit down and gather myself for a minute, which isn’t usually how I am. And even little stuff at home, like carrying groceries in from the car, feels heavier than it should. Not impossible, just… everything feels like it takes more effort to get through.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness and emptiness nearly every day?

Yeah… nearly every day, I’d say. It’s kind of become the way the day starts, which is what bothers me. I wake up and before anything has even happened, there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Not like I’m crying right away or anything, but just this… flat sadness sitting there.

I can still get up and go to my shift, and I can talk to people and do what I’m supposed to do. If someone saw me, they might think I’m basically okay because I can still answer them and be polite. But inside it feels like I’m moving through the day with everything muted. Like I’m present, but not really feeling connected to much.

It’s not that every single minute is unbearable, but most days lately, yeah, that sadness or emptiness is there in the background. Sometimes it gets quieter if I’m busy, but it doesn’t really feel gone.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I haven’t been tracking my weight closely or stepping on a scale every day or anything, so I can’t give you an exact number. My clothes don’t feel dramatically looser, at least not that I’ve noticed, and nobody’s said anything to me like I look like I’ve lost a lot of weight.

So… if I have lost any, it hasn’t been enough for me to really notice. I wouldn’t call it significant.
Have you felt less interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy doing?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I don’t think I’ve had some big, obvious loss of interest where I just stopped liking everything, if that’s what you mean.

I still know what I usually enjoy, and if someone asks me about it, I can say, yeah, I like that. But I guess I haven’t really been paying close attention to whether it feels the same when I do it. Sometimes it’s more like I go through the motions, but I don’t know if that’s because I’ve lost interest or because I’m just distracted or tired or whatever.

So… I wouldn’t want to say yes like it’s definitely happening. I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed a clear change in that way.
Would you say your low mood and other symptoms are interfering with your daily life in a mild way, or is it more significant than that?

I’d say it’s mild, but it’s not nothing, if that makes sense. Like, I’m still going to work and I’m still doing the basic things I’m supposed to do, but I can tell I’m not as dependable with details as I normally am.

At work, with my client documentation, I’ve been asking coworkers to double-check things for me more than I usually would. Not because I don’t know how to do it, but because I’ll finish it and then have this feeling like, “Did I miss something obvious?” And in my line of work, I really don’t want little mistakes slipping through.

And at home, my wife has picked up some of the bills and scheduling stuff. Normally I can keep track of that kind of thing pretty well, but lately I’m just not as reliable with the details. I’ll mean to do something and then it gets fuzzy or I second-guess whether I handled it. So… yeah, I’d call it mild interference, but it has definitely started affecting day-to-day things.
Would you say these feelings of sadness and emptiness are affecting your daily life more than just mildly?

No, I don’t think I’d say it’s more than mild. I mean, it is affecting things, and I don’t want to make it sound like there’s no impact, because there is. At work especially, I’ve noticed I’m not trusting myself with the details the way I usually do.

Like with my client documentation, I’ll get it done, but then I keep feeling like I might’ve missed something or written something down wrong, so I’ve been asking coworkers to look it over or double-check it. That’s not really typical for me, at least not this much. I can still do the work, but I need more backup than usual.

And at home, my wife has kind of stepped in with some of the bills and scheduling things, because right now I’m just not as reliable with keeping track of all that. I’ll mean to handle something, and then I’m not totally confident I did it right or remembered all the pieces.

So yeah, it’s interfering with daily life, but I’d still call it mild rather than major. It’s more like things are slipping at the edges, not that everything has fallen apart.
Would you say these feelings of sadness and emptiness are significantly impacting your ability to function at work or in your daily activities?

I wouldn’t say it’s significant in the sense that I can’t function or I’m missing work or anything like that. I’m still getting through the day and doing what I need to do.

But it is showing up in practical ways. At work, I’ve been less confident with my client documentation, so I’ve been asking coworkers to double-check it more than I normally would. I’ll finish it and then keep thinking, “Did I miss a detail? Did I write that clearly enough?” So I’m still doing it, but I’m relying on other people more.

And at home, my wife has taken over some of the bills and scheduling stuff because I’m just not as reliable with those details right now. I don’t love admitting that, because those are things I usually handle fine, but lately I need the extra help.

So I’d say it’s impacting me, yes, but I’d still put it more in the mild range than “significant.”
Would you say that most days, you've either had no interest or pleasure in doing things, or you've taken no pleasure in doing things that you normally enjoy?

I’m not totally sure I’d put it that strongly, like “no interest” or “no pleasure” most days. I mean… I’ve had times where I’m less excited about things than I think I should be, or I kind of have to push myself to get started, but I don’t know if I’d say I take no pleasure in things.

It’s more like things feel a little dulled sometimes, if that makes sense. Like I can still enjoy something once I’m doing it, but I might not look forward to it as much beforehand. So I’m hesitant to say yes to “most days” or “no pleasure,” because that sounds more intense than what I’ve noticed.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness and emptiness are present for most of the day?

Yeah… I think so, at least lately. It’s not like I’m crying all day or completely unable to talk to people, but there’s this heavy, empty feeling that’s kind of there when I wake up, like right in my chest.

I can still get up, go to my shift, talk to people, do what I’m supposed to do, and from the outside I probably seem pretty normal. But inside I feel sad and flat a lot of the day. It may ease up a little here and there if I’m distracted, but it tends to be sitting there in the background most of the time. So yes, I’d say it’s present most of the day, just more quiet and heavy than dramatic.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight, such as more than 5% of your body weight, in the past month?

I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t been tracking my weight closely or anything, and I don’t weigh myself every day, but I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting dramatically differently or people commenting that I look like I’ve lost weight.

More than 5%… I’m not even totally sure what that would be for me without doing the math, but if it was a significant amount like that, I feel like I probably would have noticed. So no, not that I’m aware of.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness and emptiness are interfering with your daily life to the point where you're having trouble doing the things you need to do?

Yeah… I’d say it’s starting to, maybe not in a completely falling-apart way, but enough that I’m noticing it and other people are noticing it.

At work, for example, I can still show up and do the care tasks, and I’m not just abandoning things, but the detail stuff has been harder. I do client documentation, and normally I’m pretty careful with that because it matters, you know? But lately I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check what I wrote, because I’ll miss something or second-guess whether I entered it correctly. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I don’t like feeling like someone has to look over my shoulder.

And at home it’s similar. My wife has been taking over more of the bills and scheduling things, appointments or just keeping track of what needs to happen, because I’m not as reliable with the details right now. I’ll think I’m going to handle something and then it kind of slips, or I just feel so heavy that I put it off and then it becomes her problem.

So I wouldn’t say I can’t function at all, but yes, it’s interfering. It’s like I’m still moving through the day, but I’m not as dependable as I usually am.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness and emptiness are causing you significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Yes… I would say it’s significant, even if I’m still technically functioning. Like, I’m not staying in bed all day or completely unable to work, but it’s definitely affecting the way I get through things.

At work, the biggest thing is the paperwork and documentation for clients. Normally I’m pretty solid with that, because it’s important and I take it seriously, but lately I’ve been asking coworkers to double-check what I’ve written or entered. Not because I don’t care, but because I don’t totally trust myself with the details right now. And that feels awful, honestly. I feel embarrassed having to ask, like I’m making extra work for other people or like I’m not doing my job the way I should.

And at home, my wife has been picking up more of the bills and scheduling stuff because I’m just not as reliable with keeping track of it. I’ll think, “Okay, I need to take care of that,” and then either I forget, or I put it off, or I get stuck in this heavy feeling and don’t follow through. So she ends up carrying more of it.

So yeah, it is causing distress. Maybe not in a dramatic way, but in a real way. It’s making me feel less dependable than I usually am, and that bothers me a lot.
